newsitem.title: USA: PSA calls Treasury yield-burning plan 'unworkable'.
newsitem.headline: PSA calls Treasury yield-burning plan 'unworkable'.

text.p: Public Securities Association Friday called "unworkable and unnecessary" a plan proposed by U.S. Treasury Department for establishing the fair market value of government securities purchased for municipal bond escrow accounts.

"The proposed rules do not provide enough certainty to issuers and dealers that the price obtained for Treasury securities will be viewed as fair market value under current law," a PSA news release said.

"Moreover, additional procedural requirements in the Treasury proposal are overly burdensome and could force participants to turn away from the open market as a source for their Treasury securities purchases,"

Following allegations that several firms had sold to municipal bond issuers Treasury securities at inflated prices, a practice known as "yield burning," Treasury proposed several methods to help government officials ensure they are getting a fair price.

But in a letter to Internal Revenue Service, PSA vice president George Brakatselos said the part of the proposal requiring comparisons with yields on reasonably comparable Treasuries "are not workable and should be deleted because they will not increase the veracity of the process."

Other comparisons called for in the rules include implied forward prices of Treasury obligations based on standard financial formulas and the yield on SLGS -- State and Local Government Series securities sold by Treasury for municipal bond escrow accounts.
PSA said those requirements represent an unnecessary burden on participants and could force issuers to purchase SLGS instead of open-market Treasuries.
"In that respect, the proposed regulations go well beyond the proper role of federal regulatory guidance," PSA stated.
PSA also said that even when dealers and issuers follow the proposed regulations, prices obtained may be challenged as "rebuttable presumptions" of fair market values.
And PSA said a proposal to prevent an underwriter from participating in the bidding process would be "difficult to satisfy" because bond syndicates can include dozens of members.
Another section of the Treasury proposal assumes that unless the yield on open-market securities is as high as the yield on SLGS, the Treasury obligations are being purchased at above-market rates.
But PSA said such a situation could arise from market fluctations during the day, since SLGS are only priced once a day.
